headline_marked: Shoriful's 6-wicket haul: [[Shoriful Islam claims 6-35]] to keep Bangladesh alive in Mackay
headline: Shoriful's 6-wicket haul: Shoriful Islam claims 6-35 to keep Bangladesh alive in Mackay
summary: After being bowled out for 64, the Tigers' left-arm pacer produced a career-best performance to dismantle Australia's top and lower order.
details: Shoriful Islam delivered a stunning comeback from injury, claiming 6 wickets for 35 runs in Mackay on Saturday. His performance turned a day of Australian dominance into one where Bangladesh can still take heart.
The Tigers were first bowled out for a meager 64 runs, with Mitchell Starc leading the attack for Australia with 6-12. However, Shoriful ensured the team was not buried on the opening day.
Shoriful struck twice in his first over, removing Travis Head and Marnus Labuschagne in five balls, leaving Australia wobbling at 41 for three.
He later broke a 77-run partnership between Steven Smith and Cameron Green by trapping Smith lbw for 42. Mehidy Hasan Miraz also contributed by removing Alex Carey.
In the final hour, Shoriful dominated the lower order, claiming three wickets in five balls, including Pat Cummins, Beau Webster, and Mitchell Starc himself.
Cameron Green's unbeaten 51 led Australia to 165 for eight at stumps. Australia currently leads by 101 runs.
Shoriful achieved a rare feat, becoming the first Test cricketer to both top-score for his team from No. 11 (with 14 runs) and take the most wickets in the opposition's innings.
The pacer attributed his success to studying videos of Australian batters and consulting with his own team's batsmen to understand the pitch conditions.
caption:
From top-scoring at No. 11 to a career-best 6-35! Shoriful Islam's incredible comeback keeps the Tigers alive.

Shoriful Islam delivered a stunning comeback from injury, claiming 6 wickets for 35 runs in Mackay on Saturday. His performance turned a day of Australian dominance into one where Bangladesh can still take heart.

The Tigers were first bowled out for a meager 64 runs, with Mitchell Starc leading the attack for Australia with 6-12. However, Shoriful ensured the team was not buried on the opening day.

Shoriful struck twice in his first over, removing Travis Head and Marnus Labuschagne in five balls, leaving Australia wobbling at 41 for three.

He later broke a 77-run partnership between Steven Smith and Cameron Green by trapping Smith lbw for 42. Mehidy Hasan Miraz also contributed by removing Alex Carey.

In the final hour, Shoriful dominated the lower order, claiming three wickets in five balls, including Pat Cummins, Beau Webster, and Mitchell Starc himself.

Cameron Green's unbeaten 51 led Australia to 165 for eight at stumps. Australia currently leads by 101 runs.

Shoriful achieved a rare feat, becoming the first Test cricketer to both top-score for his team from No. 11 (with 14 runs) and take the most wickets in the opposition's innings.

The pacer attributed his success to studying videos of Australian batters and consulting with his own team's batsmen to understand the pitch conditions.

headline_marked: 930 children dead: [[Measles outbreak death toll hits 930]] in Bangladesh
headline: 930 children dead: Measles outbreak death toll hits 930 in Bangladesh
summary: Two more children died in the last 24 hours, while 880 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), two more children died within the last 24 hours showing symptoms of measles.
The total number of deaths associated with measles symptoms since March 15 has reached 831 children.
Including 99 confirmed cases of measles, the overall death toll from both confirmed cases and symptoms has climbed to 930 children.
Additionally, 880 new patients with measles or measles-like symptoms have been admitted to hospitals nationwide in the last 24 hours.
The DGHS released these updated figures in a report on Saturday afternoon.
